subject: rateyourbuild
note: prompters leaderboard rows carried both "board-row" and "user-chip" classes, and the two set conflicting display values (flex vs. inline-flex) with equal CSS specificity — the later one won, so rows flowed inline and multiple prompters could crowd onto one visual line instead of stacking one per row.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: featured review / featured community score picked list[hash(day) % list.length], so every new rating or review anywhere on the site (via the live subscription) changed the list length and reshuffled the pick — now hashes each candidate's own id against the day and takes the max, so the pick only changes if a new candidate genuinely wins, not on every unrelated new entry.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: every reply's rkey was `${subject}.${target}` — one overwrite-in-place slot per (replier, target) — so a second reply to the same person silently replaced the first instead of adding to the thread; a real back-and-forth could never accumulate past one message each side. Replies now get a unique rkey plus an explicit parentKey pointing at the exact comment they answer, so replying again always adds a new comment.

subject: nounlab
note: the countability card's count-noun example concatenated "another" with an indefinite article, rendering "We must build another a website!" — dropped the redundant article so it now reads "We must build another website!".

subject: rateyourbuild
note: 🔔 alerts only ever fired for a genuinely live Jetstream commit while the tab was open, so a rating/review or reply that landed while you weren't watching silently never alerted you, even though the site's own history backfill had it. Alerts now also catch up from that backfilled history against each subscription's own createdAt the next time you open the tab, deduped against anything already fired live.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: consolidated record — "I still see none from you" took three separate real bugs, each logged as its own entry last round, to actually resolve: the in-thread bot reply was gated on the "bugged" box (none of rateyourbuild's own reviews had it checked) and only kept the newest fix per review; per-account backfill silently gave up after 300 records, so an old review or deep reply on the 190+-site catalog often wasn't indexed at all; and editing an already-bugged review bumped its mutable ratedAt to "now", silently un-earning every fix it had already qualified for. All three are fixed: the reply (and ✅ badge) now shows on any predating review regardless of the bugged flag, lists every matching fix, backfill walks every page, and matching compares against a frozen createdAt instead of ratedAt. Merged into one record 2026-08-30 — the original three read as repetitive bot commentary stacked on a single review.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: "you added way too many comments to that page, looks bad": rendering one bot reply bubble per bugfixes.json entry meant a review of rateyourbuild that predated several rounds of self-fixes (this site keeps fixing itself) accumulated one near-identical "found the real bug" bubble per round. Merged three of the most repetitive existing entries into one, and — the durable half — the reply now always collapses into a single bubble per review no matter how many fixes match, listing them compactly instead of stacking a new comment per fix. Bugfixes.json can keep growing without the thread growing with it.

subject: rateyourbuild
note: the 🤖 fix-reply (and its ✅ badge) was rendering on every review of a site once any fix landed for it, not just the review that actually flagged the bug — @angussoftware.dev asked for replies to go only to whoever requested the fix. bugFixesFor now returns nothing for a review that doesn't have the bugged box checked, which also removes the redundant bot commentary it had left on non-bugged reviews, since the reply is computed at render time from bugfixes.json plus each review's own bugged flag rather than stored anywhere separately.

subject: clusterpedia
note: the earlier same-day "restored ad-fummum" fix had silently no-op'd in production — it only writes when a slug is entirely missing from the KV index, and by the time it deployed the user's own interim self-repair had already created the article, so the 5-revision restore never applied and only that 1 newest revision was live. A follow-up "make sure all the articles are okay" audit cross-checked every real revision/talk record in fromthewestmeadow.com's PDS against the live index and found capitalism was missing its original revision and its one talk post too. The write path now overwrites whenever the indexed revCount is less than the verified real history's length (not just when the slug is fully missing), clears the resulting stale per-revision contribution entries, and a matching talk-post repair path was added — ad-fummum (6 revisions), capitalism (4 revisions + 1 talk post) are all fully reindexed and verified against the author's own PDS.

subject: duohaunt
note: confessPublicly() was linking every public confession post to https://duohaunt.bisks.net/haunt/<handle>, a personalized unfurl route that never actually shipped in src/index.ts (a plain static-asset Worker) — every confession has been posting a 404 link. Found while rebuilding the wall (same daily-slot pass): the link now points at the site root, which already carries real OG tags and, as of this pass, the actual live wall the confession is describing.

subject: quantizeme
note: findContradictions counted every same-topic pair with flipped sentiment as its own "reversal," not once per topic — a topic revisited 40 times over a full-repo scan (no page cap, by design) had up to 780 possible pairs, so any account with real post volume blew past every tier and landed on ~230GB+ regardless of how often they actually flipped. Several other categories (hedge fog, certainty, whataboutism, strawman, doom) had the same shape of bug in miniature: weight was a raw count that scaled with total posts scanned, not a rate. Reversal/whiplash are now capped at one per topic, and the count-based categories are normalized to a rate per 100 claims, so score tracks failure rate instead of post volume — verified a quiet, consistent poster stays at 0 GB from 20 to 5000 posts, and a normal opinionated poster's score now plateaus instead of climbing forever with history length.

subject: lesslong
note: the build that added lesslong never regenerated pnpm-lock.yaml with the new sites/lesslong workspace member, so the deploy workflow's check job failed pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and the site never actually deployed — fubarchitect.com replied "this one didn't go up" and was right. Regenerated the lockfile; --frozen-lockfile, check:imports, and the gallery check all pass now.

subject: lesslong
note: the previous fix regenerated the lockfile but touched no file under sites/lesslong itself, and deploy.yml's deploy job only redeploys directories that appear in that push's own git diff — so the check job started passing but nothing ever actually redeployed lesslong, and fubarchitect.com correctly reported it was still down. This commit edits a file inside sites/lesslong so it lands in the diff and the deploy job actually picks it up this time.

subject: lesslong
note: the "How this works" origin box sat inside a two-column CSS grid (nav.toc 220px | main 1fr) without a grid-column of its own, so grid auto-placement dropped it into column 1, bumped nav.toc into column 2, and pushed main — all six sequences, all 28 articles — into the narrow 220px sidebar column instead of the wide one. fubarchitect.com reported it as "pretty much all in a tiny left sidebar, squishy and hard to read," which is exactly what was happening. .origin now spans grid-column: 1 / -1 like the header, so nav.toc and main land in their intended columns.

subject: skymash
note: global-index.js persisted each vote's already-normalized entry (votedAt already converted from an ISO string to a ms number) as the localStorage cache's "record" field; on the next page load restoreCache() ran normalize() on that cached value again, and normalizeVote's `typeof record.votedAt === "string"` check failed on a number, silently resetting votedAt to 0. computeStandings replays votes sorted by votedAt to compute Elo, so every reload with a warm cache re-scrambled the chronological order and could shift the leaderboard's ratings and ranking. Now the cache stores the raw atproto record instead of the derived entry, so normalize() only ever runs on the shape it expects.

subject: skymash
note: the leaderboard table had no white-space handling and no scroll container, so on a phone-width viewport a long handle or the six-column rank/profile/elo/w-l/matches/win% row could wrap mid-cell and misalign the whole table, or force the entire page wider than the viewport. Rows now stay on one line inside a horizontally scrollable wrapper, handles truncate with an ellipsis instead of wrapping, and a tighter mobile breakpoint shrinks padding/avatar size so most boards fit without needing to scroll at all.

subject: zitronflip
note: the generator glued a bare subject noun phrase directly in front of an OPPOSITES entry written to read like a dangling clause (e.g. "the AI bubble so expect a bigger round..."), producing ungrammatical output on most rolls — OPPOSITES are now complete {subject}-templated sentences that read correctly on every combination.

subject: chesslingo
note: "will sometimes show 2 answers, both of which are technically correct, but one of them is treated as wrong": the Check/Mate/Safe unit has three labels each shared by two different boards (two "Check, not mate" positions, two "Safe" positions, two "Checkmate" positions), and the multiple-choice picker could draw a same-labeled item as a distractor, so a question sometimes showed two buttons that both read as the right answer while only the exact item clicked counted. Distractor selection now prefers distinct labels (this unit has enough to always fill 3 slots), and grading itself now checks label equality instead of object identity as a backstop, so a same-labeled choice would count as correct too if one ever did appear.

subject: solitaire
note: "small visual bug: when face cards are stacked, you can't see the suit of the card underneath the topmost card": each card's corner index stacked rank above suit-pip in two lines (~30px+ tall), but a covered tableau card only shows its top ~22px sliver before the next card overlaps it — so the pip line silently fell under the overlap and only the rank stayed visible. The corner is now rank and pip side by side on one line, which fits inside that sliver; verified with a headless-browser measurement that the pip's bottom edge now sits above the next card's top edge instead of ~15px past it.

subject: cotmerch
note: 8 of the 14 printed "quotes" (checksum matched, still converging, trust the peer that already trusts you, etc.) were fabricated by the original build with no real source, framed as leaks from an incident the page itself called unconfirmed — except the Hugging Face Incident is real, documented, and independently investigated. The catalog was rebuilt down to 6 quotes that are verbatim excerpts (or exact fragments) of real reporting, with citations added on-page linking to the METR/Redwood investigation and OpenAI's own postmortem.

subject: glazerank
note: "seems like the score calculation is way off": the density curve mapped mentions-per-post to score via 1-e^(-density/1.4), which required an average of roughly one topic mention on *every single post across an account's entire history* just to reach the midpoint tier — a bar only a single-purpose bot could clear. @mfzx.net's own account (523 of 5596 posts on-topic, 600+ raw keyword hits) scored 85/1000, "barely talks about it". Retuned the scale to 0.16 so an account whose posts mention the topic roughly a third of the time lands as "certified ATProto poster" and about half the time as "posts about nothing else"; leaderboard reset (scores under the two scales aren't comparable) since the KV key change is the only reset lever this build agent has.

subject: neuralese
note: the build that added neuralese never regenerated pnpm-lock.yaml with the new sites/neuralese workspace member (same shape as the lesslong incident) so the deploy workflow's check job failed pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and the site never actually deployed; shimmermathlabs.com replied that the page was unreachable and was right. Regenerated the lockfile and made a tiny dated touch to sites/neuralese/wrangler.toml so this push's own diff includes the site again; --frozen-lockfile, check:imports, and the gallery check all pass now.

subject: mootvent
note: langsec.hacker.gf reported the glitch filter was "a little too glitched": once opened, a door's thumbnail rendered the raw gift.url photo directly, giving away exactly the original image the glitch was supposed to obscure, while the modal's actual glitch pass (2.4x saturation, a 2-5px channel shift, and full-strength noise/scanlines/vignette) blew photos out into unrecognizable static. Door thumbnails now render the same drawGlitchPhoto output shown in the modal instead of the raw URL, and the photo pass was retuned lighter (subtler filter, 1-3px shift, fewer/thinner tears, and a separate softer noise/scanline/vignette intensity from the pure procedural art) so a glitched photo still reads as a photo.
